# Data Cleaning

## Recollecting Events

```{r import.affect.scores}

#In this section we import wisdom and emotion scores from event recollection

#Set working directory to where the recollection file is located
setwd("C:\\Users\\mypc\\Dropbox\\Community 1.0 Raw Files\\CSV\\")

#setwd("C:\\Users\\igrossma\\Dropbox\\Community 1.0 Raw Files\\CSV\\")

#Import recollection data

recollection.demo.cond.wiz <- read.csv("C:\\Users\\mypc\\Dropbox\\Community 1.0 Raw Files\\CSV\\forecasting.analysis.wisdom_May7_2019.csv", stringsAsFactors = F)

```


```{r subset.recollection}

#In this section we drop empty rows for participants who did not report any events during the course of the study. 

community.affective <- subset(recollection.demo.cond.wiz, refl.event > 1)

```


```{r preparation.affect.scores}

#In this segment we recode event, emotion, time and event variables

#Declare Factors
community.affective$PID <- factor(community.affective$subjectNumber)
community.affective$Event <- factor(community.affective$Event)

#Check number of events by type of event
table(community.affective$Event)

#Create positive and negative dummy codes for type of events
community.affective$Eventpos[community.affective$Event == "Argument"] <- 0
community.affective$Eventpos[community.affective$Event == "Betrayal"] <- 0
community.affective$Eventpos[community.affective$Event == "Exclusion"] <- 0
community.affective$Eventpos[community.affective$Event == "Gathering"] <- 1
community.affective$Eventpos[community.affective$Event == "Pleasant Conversation"] <- 1
community.affective$Eventpos[community.affective$Event == "Support"] <- 1


#Create factor version of the dummy coded event variable
community.affective$Eventpos_F <- factor(community.affective$Eventpos, labels=c("Negative", "Positive"))

#Check Condition codes
table(community.affective$Condition.D)

#Recode Condition
community.affective$cond[community.affective$Condition.D == 1] <- 0
community.affective$cond[community.affective$Condition.D == 3] <- 1

#Create a factor version of the condition variable
community.affective$cond_F <- factor(community.affective$cond, labels = c("First Person", "Third Person"))

#Check frequency of emotion terms
table(community.affective$Emotion)

#Dummy code emotion terms into positive and negative
community.affective$Emopos[community.affective$Emotion == "Angry"] <- 0
community.affective$Emopos[community.affective$Emotion == "Frustrated"] <- 0
community.affective$Emopos[community.affective$Emotion == "Upset"] <- 0
community.affective$Emopos[community.affective$Emotion == "Content"] <- 1
community.affective$Emopos[community.affective$Emotion == "Liking"] <- 1
community.affective$Emopos[community.affective$Emotion == "Trustful"] <- 1

#Create a factor version for emotions and label the dummy codes
community.affective$Emopos_F <- factor(community.affective$Emopos, labels = c("Negative", "Positive"))

#Convert PrePost vector to numeric and dummy code it
community.affective$PrePost_N[community.affective$PrePost == "Pre"] <- 0
community.affective$PrePost_N[community.affective$PrePost == "Post"] <- 1

```

## Mood and Feeling to Close Others Accuracy

```{r subset.aff.social}

#Subsets for mood accuracy (happy only) and social emotions accuracy (emotions with social action tendencies)

community.affect <- subset(community.affective, Emotion == "Happy")

community.social <- subset(community.affective, !Emotion == "Happy")

```


```{r mean.center.aff.social}

#In this section we mean mean-center all predictors for both community.social and community.affect and also Normalize the scores (since the variable is heavily skewed)

#Community Affect

#Mean center
community.affect$Eventpos_C <- scale(community.affect$Eventpos,scale = F)
community.affect$cond_C <- scale(community.affect$cond,scale = F)
community.affect$Emopos_C <- scale(community.affect$Emopos,scale = F)
community.affect$PrePost_C <- scale(community.affect$PrePost_N, scale = F)
community.affect$diffwiz_C <- scale(community.affect$diff.wiz,scale = F)

#Check distribution
#hist(community.affect$Score) #variable skewed so need to normalize

#Fix happy for the forecasting dataset
community.affect[community.affect$PrePost_N == 0 , c("Score.fixed")] <- community.affect[community.affect$PrePost_N == 0 , c("Score")] - 4

community.affect$Score.fixed <- ifelse(community.affect$PrePost_N == 1, community.affect$Score, community.affect$Score.fixed)

#Normalize
community.affect$score.norm <- Normalize(community.affect$Score.fixed)

#hist(community.affect$score.norm) 

#Community Social

#Mean center
community.social$Eventpos_C <- scale(community.social$Eventpos,scale = F)
community.social$cond_C <- scale(community.social$cond,scale = F)
community.social$Emopos_C <- scale(community.social$Emopos,scale = F)
community.social$PrePost_C <- scale(community.social$PrePost_N, scale = F)
community.social$diffwiz_C <- scale(community.social$diff.wiz,scale = F)

#Check distribution
#hist(community.social$Score) #variable skewed so need to normalize

#Normalize
community.social$score.norm <- Normalize(community.social$Score)

```



## Forecasting

```{r import.probab.scores}

#In this segment we import affective forecasting probability scores 

forecasting.prob.demo.cond.wiz <- read.csv("C:\\Users\\mypc\\Dropbox\\Community 1.0 Raw Files\\CSV\\forecasting.analysis.probability_May7_2019.csv", stringsAsFactors = F)



```


```{r subset.forecasting}

#In this section we drop empty rows for participants who did not report any events during the course of the study. 

forecast.probab <- subset(forecasting.prob.demo.cond.wiz, refl.event > 1)

```


```{r preparation.probability.scores}

#In this section we declare factors and dummy code event and condition variables

#Declare factors
forecast.probab$PID <- factor(forecast.probab$subjectNumber)
forecast.probab$Event <- factor(forecast.probab$Scenario)

#Create positive and negative dummy codes for type of events
forecast.probab$Eventpos[forecast.probab$Event == "Argument"] <- 0
forecast.probab$Eventpos[forecast.probab$Event == "Betrayal"] <- 0
forecast.probab$Eventpos[forecast.probab$Event == "Exclusion"] <- 0
forecast.probab$Eventpos[forecast.probab$Event == "Gathering"] <- 1
forecast.probab$Eventpos[forecast.probab$Event == "Pleasant Conversation"] <- 1
forecast.probab$Eventpos[forecast.probab$Event == "Support"] <- 1


#Create factor version of the event variable
forecast.probab$Eventpos_F <- factor(forecast.probab$Eventpos)

#Check Condition
table(forecast.probab$Condition.D)

#Recode Condition
forecast.probab$cond[forecast.probab$Condition.D == 1] <- 0
forecast.probab$cond[forecast.probab$Condition.D == 3] <- 1

#Create factor version of the condition variable
forecast.probab$cond_F <- factor(forecast.probab$cond)

```



```{r mean.centering.prediction.scores}

#In this section we mean center all predictors for the forecasting dataset.

forecast.probab$Eventpos_C <- scale(forecast.probab$Eventpos, scale = F)
forecast.probab$cond_C <- scale(forecast.probab$cond, scale = F)
forecast.probab$diffwiz_C <- scale(Normalize(forecast.probab$diff.wiz), scale = F)
forecast.probab$AFPProb_C <- scale(forecast.probab$AFPProb, scale = F)


```

# Analyses in the paper

## Effect of Condition

```{r tests.for.social.forecasting}

#In this section we test the effect of Time, Condition, Emotion Type and Event Type on emotion scores

#Model fit
testS1 <- lme4::lmer(Normalize(Score) ~ (1|PID) + PrePost_C * cond_C * Emopos_C * Eventpos_C, data = community.social)

#View Summary 1
summary(testS1)

#View Summary 2
Anova(testS1, type = "III")

```


```{r subset.event.type}

#In this section we subset community.social into positive and negative events

community.social.negsit <- subset(community.social, Eventpos_F == "Negative")
community.social.possit <- subset(community.social, Eventpos_F == "Positive")

```

## Positive Events

```{r analyses.positive.events}

#In this section we test the effect of Time, Condition and Emotion Type on Emotion for positive events only. 

testS2.pos <- lmer(Normalize(Score) ~ (1|PID) + scale(PrePost_C, scale = F) * scale(cond_C, scale = F) * scale(Emopos_C, scale = F), data = community.social.possit)

#View Summary 1
summary(testS2.pos)

#View Summary 2
Anova(testS2.pos, type="III") 

#Result - interaction is not significant.


```

## Negative Events

```{r analyses.negative.events}

#In this section we test the effect of Time, Condition and Emotion Type on Emotion using rows for negative events only. 

#Mean Centering Emotion type, Time and Condition variables
community.social.negsit$Emopos_C <- as.numeric(scale(community.social.negsit$Emopos_C, scale = F))

community.social.negsit$PrePost_C <- as.numeric(scale(community.social.negsit$PrePost_C, scale = F))

community.social.negsit$cond_C <- as.numeric(scale(community.social.negsit$cond_C, scale = F))


#Normalize Score
community.social.negsit$score.norm <- Normalize(community.social.negsit$Score)

#Fit model
testS2.neg <- lmer(score.norm ~ (1|PID) + PrePost_C * cond_C * Emopos_C,  data = community.social.negsit)

#View Summary 1
summary(testS2.neg)

#View Summary 2
Anova(testS2.neg, type = "III") 

#Result : sig 3 way!

#Plot

plot1.neg <- cat_plot(testS2.neg, cond_C, PrePost_C, Emopos_C, geom = "point", interval.geom = "errorbar", centered = "all", robust = T, pred.labels = c("First Person", "Third Person"), modx.labels = c("Forecast", "Experience"), mod2.labels = c("Negative Emotions", "Positive Emotions"), x.label = "Condition", y.label = "Emotional Intensity + /- 95 CI", color.class = "Set1")

plotA <- plot1.neg + theme_hc() + 
 scale_color_viridis(discrete = TRUE, option = "D", direction = -1) + theme(legend.title = element_blank(), legend.justification = c(1, 0), legend.position = c(1, 0.7))

plotA

#Check simple effects

jtools::sim_slopes(testS2.neg, PrePost_C, cond_C, mod2 = Emopos_C, centered = "all", digits = 3)

jtools::sim_slopes(testS2.neg, cond_C, Emopos_C, mod2 = PrePost_C, centered = "all", digits = 3)

```



```{r mean.center.normalize.social}

#In this section we mean center and normalize emotion and wisdom scores from 2 separate data.frames

community.social.possit$score.norm <- Normalize(community.social.possit$Score)
community.social.possit$diffwiz_C <- scale(community.social.possit$diffwiz, scale = F)
community.social.negsit$diffwiz_C <- scale(community.social.negsit$diffwiz, scale = F)

```

## Wisdom Growth

```{r analyses.wisdom.growth}

#In this section we test the effect of Growth in Wise Reasoning, Time, Event type and Emotion Type on Emotion Scores.

#Fit Model
testS5 <- lmer(score.norm ~ (1|PID) + diffwiz_C * PrePost_C * Emopos_C * Eventpos_C, data = community.social)

#Summary 1
summary(testS5)

summ(testS5, center = "all", digits = 4)

#Summary 2
Anova(testS5, type = "III")

#Plot model
interact_plot(testS5, PrePost_C, diffwiz_C, mod2 = Emopos_C, centered = "all", interval = T, robust = T, int.width = .8, x.label = "Forecasted vs. Experienced", pred.labels = c("Forecast", "Exper."), mod2.labels = c("Negative Emotions", "Positive Emotions"), legend.main = "Growth in Wise Reasoning", color.class = "Qual1")

```

## Positive Events

```{r analyses.wisdom.growth.positive.sit}

#In this section we examine the effect of wisdom growth, Time and Emotion Type for positive situations.

###POSITIVE SITUATIONS

#Model Fit
testS6 <- lmer(score.norm ~ (1|PID) + diffwiz_C * PrePost_C * Emopos_C, data = community.social.possit)

#View Summary 1
summary(testS6)

#View Summary 2
Anova(testS6, type = "III") 

#Result: no effect

#Plot model
interact_plot(testS6, PrePost_C, diffwiz_C, mod2 = Emopos_C, centered = "all", interval = T, robust = T, int.width = .8, x.label = "Forecasted vs. Experienced", pred.labels = c("Forecast", "Exper."), mod2.labels = c("Negative Emotions", "Positive Emotions"), legend.main = "Growth in Wise Reasoning", color.class = "Qual1")

```

# Supplemental Section

```{r tests.for.predictions, eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}

testP1 <- glmer(AFP.dummy ~ (1|PID) + (1|Event) + AFPProb_C * cond_C * Eventpos_C, data = forecast.probab, family = binomial, glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 100000)))

summary(testP1) #prediction is more accurate in the third vs. first person condition. Event is also more likely to happen for pos third person vs. neg first person. marginal effects, though.

test.1.values <- ggeffects::ggpredict(testP1, c("AFPProb_C", "cond_C"))

plot(test.1.values)

interact_plot(testP1, AFPProb_C, cond_C, mod2 = Eventpos_C, centered = "all", interval = T, robust = T, int.width = .8, x.label	= "Predicted Likelihood", y.label = "Event Likelihood (log)", legend.main = "Condition", modx.labels = c("First Person", "Third Person"), color.class = "Qual1") + theme(legend.title = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom") + theme_gdocs() + theme(legend.title = element_blank(), legend.position = "top") 

#examine effects for wise reasoning components
testP4 <- glmer(AFP.dummy ~ (1|PID) + (1|Event) + AFPProb_C * scale(Normalize(diffwiz_C), scale = F) * Eventpos_C, data = forecast.probab, family = binomial, glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 100000)))

summary(testP4)

interact_plot(testP4, AFPProb_C, diffwiz_C, mod2 = Eventpos_C, centered = "all", interval = T, robust = T, int.width = .8, x.label = "Likelihood", pred.labels = c("Forecast", "Exper."), mod2.labels = c("Negative Sit", "Positive Sit"), legend.main = "Growth in Wise Reasoning", color.class = "Qual1") 

#nothing for neg events, but greater accuracy in predictions for positive events among those who experienced growth between time 1 and time 2

```


## Affective Forecasting using Happy only

```{r tests.for.affective.forecasting}

#In this section we test the effect of Time, Condition and Event type on Emotion.

#Fit the model
test1 <- lme4::lmer(score.norm ~ PrePost_C + (1|PID), data = community.affect)

#View Summary 1
summary(test1)

#View Summary 2
Anova(test1,type="III")

#Result: no effect of condition for happy, though a main effect of event positivity vs. negativity

#Main Effects Model
test1a <- lmer(score.norm ~ (1|PID) + PrePost_C , data = community.affect)

#View Summary 1
summary(test1a)

#View Summary 2
Anova(test1a,type="III")

summ(test1a)

```
